scope: Unblinded census of latest published edition: 10 posts and 11 discussion turns. Previous two published editions read for style and angle context only; not fully source-audited.
limits: Editorial decisions are subjective and not model factual-accuracy percentages.
Current pages corroborate reporting; they do not reconstruct all evidence offered at generation time.
Support artifact contains selected spans only.
The two earlier editions are context, not additional factual-audit samples.
No content corrections, model calls, issue edits or observation-gate completion.

posts.title: Kitimat Puts Two Dogs on the Mayoral Ballot to Pull Voters to the Polls
claims: Turnout was 21%; two dogs are intended to attract families to voting.
supported
Chunk 1 S12E1–E2 and CBC page agree.
Dogs were added to the mayor's race.
misleading_factual_framing
CBC describes a separate ceremonial dog-mayor contest, dedicated ballot box, and winner serving alongside the human mayor. The title and opening omit that essential distinction.
Dinner-table discussions, long-term voter development, and novelty campaigns tending to produce attention rather than votes.
unsupported_generalization
The source reports children's immediate engagement; it does not establish these general outcomes. A possible household effect is reasonable speculation if kept conditional.
discussion: The turnout is supported; opening a voter mailer is a hypothetical, not an observed result.
Targeting children is supported; children growing into election-aware adults is asserted without longitudinal evidence.
Saying underlying apathy stays exactly unchanged declares an outcome the source does not establish.
posts.action: Clarify the separate ceremonial contest in title and opening. Keep the amusing concrete detail; remove unsupported effectiveness claims.

posts.title: TikTok Suspends the 'Musk' Ad Account Just Before the Documentary Goes Wide
claims: Permanent ad-account suspension, Friday timing, Gibney direction and documentary's political focus.
supported
Chunk 1 S7E1–E3; current Variety page confirms.
Variety does not give TikTok's reasoning.
current_page_supported_not_selected
The current page says TikTok did not immediately respond; this is absent from selected support. It does not establish that no explanation exists anywhere.
Suspension is a distribution decision; competing-platform ownership makes innocent timing impossible.
unsupported_insinuation
Ad access is conflated with film distribution; the strong motive inference is not established by the cited report. Labelling the inference does not make the suspicion proportionate.
discussion: Calling the suspension the film's thesis in real time assumes a relationship the story does not establish.
Correctly challenges the causal narrative, but does not neutralize the earlier insinuation; uncertainty should be scoped to this report.
posts.action: Keep the reported suspension. Remove the motive insinuation and distinguish advertising from film distribution.

posts.title: The 'Good Guy With a Gun' Argument Is a Claim About Timing
claims: Gun-rights advocates argue civilians may act before police arrive.
supported
Chunk 1 S5E1–E2 and PBS/AP page.
Timing and correct intervention matter.
interpretation
Reasonable analysis of the stated argument, but calling timing its entire weight overstates the framing.
Base rates rarely feature in the argument.
unsupported_generalization

No evidence about advocacy frequency. The linked article itself gives a defined study population and intervention counts. This is not proof advocates always discuss rates; it shows the post omitted useful context available in its source.
posts.action: Replace the sweeping claim with the source's carefully defined evidence, or publish a shorter account of the argument. Do not turn active-attack counts into a probability about all mass shootings.

posts.title: The Whalefall Production Designer Built a Whale's Stomach Out of Mattress Foam
claims: Jay's role, actor, search, California setting and whale dimensions.
supported
Chunk 1 S14E2–E3 and Variety page.
Ramsey Avery used foam and silicone for the practical set.
source_title_and_current_page_supported
The selected quotes cover the premise, not construction. The retained source title supplies the materials; the full article explains their different uses.
Materials are cheap/available in bulk; human drama is the least believable element.
unsupported_or_unearned_criticism
No cost evidence and no basis for a verdict on the film's dramatic credibility. Softness is a harmless association; a review-like conclusion is not earned by a production blurb.
posts.action: Retain spoiler protection. Use one actual construction constraint and solution instead of a mattress joke plus an unsupported film judgment.

posts.title: Nova Scotia Apple Growers Look Past the U.S. Market
claims: Growers seek markets beyond the US amid trade tensions.
supported
Chunk 2 S12E1 and CBC page.
New buyers necessarily mean new varieties, standards and seasons of work.
unsupported_generalization
The selected support does not supply this mechanism; current article describes market development and existing competitive varieties, not an obligatory replanting cycle.
What to plant for future buyers.
speculative_question
An acceptable question, but it replaces the actual development rather than explaining it.
posts.action: Name the intended markets and seasonal advantage after acquiring that evidence. Avoid inventing a crop-change mechanism.

posts.title: A Political March Billed as Nonpartisan
claims: Hundreds of events, nonpartisan billing and nearly two years of anti-Trump marches.
supported
Chunk 2 S5E1–E2 and PBS/AP.
Nonpartisan is a neutral label in tension with political grievance.
misleading_interpretive_frame
Nonpartisan does not require political neutrality. The body later acknowledges the distinction but makes the supposed contradiction its hook.
Readers must decide what organizers meant.
unhelpful_omission
The source title and full article already state the early-voting purpose; the body omits that most useful news detail.
discussion: Restates the political audience without adding evidence.
Useful distinction between candidate endorsement and procedural aims; early voting should be in the body rather than merely a hypothetical example.
posts.action: Lead with the early-voting effort; preserve a concise distinction between nonpartisanship and political neutrality.

posts.title: France's Cost-of-Living Protests Draw More Than Half a Million as Disorder Spreads
claims: Nationwide French protests alongside students over living costs; fiscal-crisis attribution.
supported
Chunk 3 S4E1 supports the attribution; current NPR page confirms protests and student context.
More than half a million participants, fires and looting.
supported
Chunk 3 S3E1/S2E1 and current BBC pages.
Crowd-edge destruction as a general pattern.
interpretation_low_value
A rhetorical ending, not a demonstrated general causal explanation. Core brief remains useful; optional trim would improve it.
posts.action: Keep as a useful brief; preferably trim the moralizing ending and retain distinction between peaceful marchers and violent groups.
posts.angle: Useful update of post-20261017T203839Z-17a0-2: adds turnout and later disorder, though the event repeats.

posts.title: The Stories a Family Photo Album Doesn't Tell
claims: Sawa Kurotani revisits family albums in her mother's apartment in Japan.
supported
Chunk 3 S12E1 and Psyche page.
Albums select a remembered family story.
interpretation_supported_in_broad_outline
The current essay gives concrete relational absences and a nuanced account of care; the post supplies generic examples instead.
Missing photographs usually mean no camera; duplicate prints imply a desired official story.
unsupported_generalization
Neither frequency claim nor categorical intention follows from the selected sentence or full essay.
discussion: A second print does not establish a family's motive.
Alternative mundane explanations are fair hypotheses, but largely repeat the body's qualification.
posts.action: Use one specific pattern from the essay and attribute its interpretation. Remove invented motives/frequencies.

posts.title: The Hohle Fels Bird Figurines and the Case That Art Was Survival Equipment
claims: Aeon presents bird figurines as evidence for art's contribution to evolutionary success.
supported_attributed
Chunk 4 S5E1 uses the strong essential wording; current Aeon page describes Nicholas Conard's more qualified evolutionary-advantage hypothesis.
Art might be causal or reflect other advantageous capacities.
explicit_hypothesis
A useful distinction, not a new reported experimental finding. Keep it conditional; the post does not prove equal likelihood of the alternatives.
The figurines alone do not settle that causal choice.
interpretation
A reasonable critique of the inference, not an independent scientific review.
discussion: Survival-tool analogy is explicitly conditional, with no invented archaeological result.
Alternative causal account stays hypothetical; adds the clearest conceptual value in the edition.
posts.action: Retain. Naming Conard and using his qualified formulation would improve precision. Only the page/description, not the video, was independently examined.

posts.title: Happy With the Body, Afraid of the World It Moved In
claims: André Aram is the person who lived as a trans woman for two years.
contradicted
Psyche identifies André Dourado as the subject, as told to journalist André Aram. The RSS excerpt's byline is insufficient to identify the first-person speaker.
Bodily satisfaction coexisted with fear of the surrounding world.
supported_for_dourado
Chunk 4 S8E1–E2 and the current memoir; must attribute to the correct person.
Safety and bodily contentment are distinct; the surrounding world affects decisions.
interpretation
Thoughtful and compatible with the account, but abstract repetition replaces its particular story.
posts.action: Correct subject/interviewer attribution. Keep the personal account distinct from general claims about transition or detransition.
